evidence.text:
Originally phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ʔljin): phonetic 𠂈 (OC *l'ɯːnʔ) + semantic 貝 (“cowry”); 𠂈 (a knife or dagger) was then a phonetic component. Often 丁 (OC *rteːŋ, *teːŋ) (a nail) was added as a second phonetic component at the bottom; originally, it appeared as a black dot. He Linyi posits it to be the original character for 珍 (OC *ʔl'ɯn, “rare; valuable”).
The sound component 𠂈 corrupted into 十 in the modern form, and into 匕 in the orthodox seal script form 眞. The bottom of the character in both forms derives from the components 貝 and 丁 corrupting into 目 and 丌.
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan; cognate with Tibetan བདེན (bden, “true; truth”). Possibly connected with 貞 (OC *teŋ) (Schuessler, 2007).

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解; 字形; early usage
evidence.text: The database reports no oracle-bone form and identifies 真 in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions. It describes bronze forms as using 貝 with 𠂈 as a phonetic element; some forms instead use 鼎, which it says is graphically confusable with 貝 in ancient component use, and one 真盤 form adds 丌. It reports bronze 真 used in a personal name. These are the database's account of the record and analysis, not independent visual inspection of the inscription images.
evidence.kind: character-specific lexicographic/paleographic reference
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 真

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解; proposed original sense and phonetic form
evidence.text: The reference identifies 𠂈 with the ancient graph associated with 殄 and 顛, and proposes that 真 may be the original graph for 珍, ‘precious’. It attributes this proposal to 何琳儀, and also reports a proposal by 謝明文: 真 was borrowed for the word ‘true’, after which 珍 was formed with 玉 as semantic marker and 㐱 as phonetic marker. This is a reported analysis, not a settled derivation. The page gives no independent reconstruction for the name of an object supposedly depicted by 𠂈; the sound-component account does not require such an object-name claim.
evidence.kind: character-specific lexicographic reference reporting competing analyses
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 真

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The page cites the Qin Shuihudi legal-question bamboo manuscript (睡虎地秦簡, slip 49) for 真 in the sense ‘actual/true’ in a legal discussion, and cites 莊子《秋水》 and 呂氏春秋《上農》 for ‘original nature’ or ‘inherent nature’. It also cites 荀子《非十二字》 for adverbial ‘indeed’. These citations show distinct textual uses, but the page does not establish their exact dates of composition or manuscript copying in this entry; the early Western Zhou bronze personal-name use does not by itself prove the same spoken sense.
evidence.kind: character-specific lexicographic reference citing primary texts
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 真

evidence.source: 《常用漢字二百字探源》, entry 134, 真
evidence.text: This paleographic study says 真 is not attested in oracle-bone inscriptions and first appears in Western Zhou bronzes. Its description distinguishes a form from 貝 and 𠂈, another with an added lower 丌 element, and forms with 鼎. It traces later graphic changes, including 貝 becoming 目-like in Spring and Autumn forms and subsequent Warring States changes. It presents 唐蘭's analysis of 真 as an early graph related to 殄 and says the early 鼎/真 graphs have been argued to be confusable. This provides a graphic-history account, but the article's excerpted discussion does not resolve the competing lexical-origin proposals.
evidence.kind: paleographic study
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源（entry 134 真）

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 online text and 段玉裁《說文解字注》
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry glosses 眞 as an immortal transforming shape and ascending to heaven, analyzing it through 𠤎, 目, 乚 and 八. Duan Yucai's later annotation treats this as the original meaning and says the classics use the graph for ‘sincere’; he further explains later senses and sound-series characters. These are historical philological interpretations, not direct evidence for the Western Zhou graph's original referent. The Shuowen entry's graph is 眞, while the modern standard graph is 真.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text with later commentary
evidence.title: 說文解字「眞」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; dated textual citations
evidence.text: The dictionary repeats the Shuowen explanation, identifies the seal-script structure as 匕, 目, 乚 and 八, and notes that today's standard form 真 takes a popular graphic form with an upper portion written like 直. Its sense section cites Zhuangzi, Warring States-era texts, the Han Shu, and later works for meanings including immortal/person, inherent nature, portrait, substantive appointment, regular script, genuine, and adverbial ‘indeed’. The entries provide citations but do not establish a complete chronology of semantic change; the sequence cannot be inferred from their gloss list.
evidence.kind: official character-variant dictionary
evidence.title: A02768 真 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 異體字研訂; 金文形體傳承
evidence.text: The dictionary's entry for variant 𡙊 reports that forms cited from 季真鬲 and 真盤 have an upper 匕-like shape and lower 鼎-like shape, and proposes that the small-seal form developed from such bronze forms. This is a specific proposed graphic relationship in the dictionary; it does not by itself settle whether the early graph's lexical origin was ‘true’, ‘precious’, or another word.
evidence.kind: official character-variant dictionary reporting a paleographic proposal
evidence.title: A02768-002 𡙊 (真) — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 〈「誠」、「真」互涵與會通的觀念史研究〉, 東亞觀念史集刊 10 (2016)
evidence.field: early graphic interpretation; textual history of 真人
evidence.text: The article reports a proposal that early bronze 真 forms may have arisen through confusion with 鼎 and advances a speculative account connecting the graph to a ritual/alchemical cauldron and later ideas of immortality. It states that 真人 is first found in the extant textual record in Zhuangzi, while distinguishing that textual history from the graph's formation. Its own proposal is not confirmation that the bronze forms depict a cauldron or that the form was created for the immortal sense.
evidence.kind: scholarly historical study discussing a disputed interpretation
evidence.title: 「誠」、「真」互涵與會通的觀念史研究

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.
